audit.whatIsWrong: diff read EVEN while diffRating said 8/10 and both difficulty lines said 'Hard matchup'. The chart also gave level 1 and levels 4-5 to 'Skill' and handed Olaf both item rows.
audit.why: Sylas wins 44.29% here — this is a losing lane, and diff should say so. Olaf owns level 1 onward (1000-range slow on a 9s cooldown that resets on pickup, against a melee with a delayed AoE); the packet chart and the mirror olaf__sylas both give the item rows back to Sylas as his AP and Kingslayer healing outscale a true-damage ramp.
audit.corrected: diff to HARD; rows 1, 4-5, first item and 2+ items flipped in matched pairs to Olaf / Olaf / Skill / Sylas, ratings moved, three phase whys rewritten.

audit.why: Four spikes, correctly ordered — his level 2-3 axe loop, the level 6 double-Ragnarok standoff, his first-item true damage, and Sylas's late scaling. Only the ability named inside spikes[0] was wrong.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text renamed to Tough It Out and Berserker Rage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields call Olaf's W 'Vicious Strikes' and describe it as lifesteal. Four fields say Abduct stuns, and wants.foe[1] tells the reader Ragnarok makes that stun whiff.
audit.why: Olaf's W is Tough It Out (700 range, 16/15/14/13/12s): attack speed plus a shield. The lifesteal is Berserker Rage, his passive, and it scales with his missing health — which is the opposite advice, because chunking him makes him stronger, not weaker. Sylas's Abduct is a chain that pulls him to the target with no stun; Ragnarok grants immunity to disables while he keeps attacking, so what it actually beats is the Chain Lash slow, not a stun that does not exist.
audit.corrected: W renamed and re-described as a shield, the lifesteal attributed to the passive with its missing-health scaling stated, and Ragnarok's real interaction written in place of the phantom stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls a spent Undertow a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Undertow is a flat 9 seconds at every rank, and picking the axe back up resets it outright — the window is shorter than advertised and can vanish entirely.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to nine seconds; the pickup-denial advice already present elsewhere is what makes it real.

audit.why: The packet flagged 'His Reckless Swing' as a suspect name; it is a false positive — Reckless Swing is the correct name of Olaf's E, and the true-damage description matches the kit.

edits.before: At level 1 Olaf simply throws his axe (Undertow) and walks onto you — his slow lasts long enough that your only level-1 tool, Q, cannot re-establish range. Stand behind minions so the axe hits creeps first, and do not step up to contest his CS unless the axe is visibly on the ground waiting for his pickup. At level 2 his Vicious Strikes (W) activates lifesteal and attack speed; if he picks up the axe he loops Undertow almost immediately and the slow chain never drops. These two levels belong to him: last-hit safely, track where the axe lands, and hold your E charges for escape, not aggression. At level 3 your full kit is online but his is more dangerous than yours — his E deals true damage every few seconds independent of your resistances, while your Q slow requires him to stand still long enough to be hooked. Only trade when Undertow is down and you are near full HP.
edits.after: At level 1 Olaf simply throws his axe (Undertow) and walks onto you — his slow lasts long enough that your only level-1 tool, Q, cannot re-establish range. Stand behind minions so the axe hits creeps first, and do not step up to contest his CS unless the axe is visibly on the ground waiting for his pickup. At level 2 his Tough It Out (W) gives him attack speed and a shield; if he picks up the axe he resets Undertow outright and the slow chain never drops. These two levels belong to him: last-hit safely, track where the axe lands, and hold your E charges for escape, not aggression. At level 3 your full kit is online but his is more dangerous than yours — his E deals true damage every 7-11 seconds regardless of your resistances, while your Q slow requires him to stand still long enough to be chained. Only trade when Undertow is down and you are near full HP.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 the lane remains his if he plays the axe correctly. Your only real agency is the E2 hook window: when Undertow is on cooldown (roughly 9 seconds early on, shrinking with CDR) you can E1 forward, chain E2 onto him, Q for the slow, and W for the burst-heal burst. That is your entire pattern, and it requires him to have missed or thrown the axe before you commit. If he has the axe in hand or on the ground nearby, do not E2 — he slow-chains you, activates W lifesteal, and true-damages you through the extended trade faster than your W can compensate. Respect the pickup spot: standing on where the axe lands denies his reset and collapses his loop; it is worth losing a minion or two to achieve. At level 6 both of you gain CC immunity via Ragnarok — his lets him ignore your E2 stun, yours gives you the same insurance. The fight is now a pure damage and sustain check; small HP and gold leads from surviving early are the entire margin.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 the lane remains his if he plays the axe correctly. Your only real agency is the Abduct window: when Undertow is on cooldown (a flat 9 seconds, shrinking with haste) you can E1 forward, chain E2 onto him, Q for the slow, and W for the burst-heal. That is your entire pattern, and it requires him to have missed or thrown the axe before you commit. If he has the axe in hand or on the ground nearby, do not chain in — he slow-loops you, shields with W, and true-damages you through the extended trade faster than your heal can compensate. Respect the pickup spot: standing where the axe lands denies his reset and collapses his loop; it is worth losing a minion or two. At level 6 Ragnarok makes him immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking, so your Q slow simply stops applying. The fight is a pure damage and sustain check; small HP and gold leads from surviving early are the entire margin.

edits.before: Two items in, the matchup finally tips. Your AP and W healing compound past his true-damage scaling; stolen Ragnarok means his all-in no longer shuts off your kit; and your chain-passive auto burst in a prolonged brawl outlasts his Vicious Strikes uptime. The realistic path here is: survive lane without falling more than one kill behind, control vision so he cannot run off to side-lane freely, and take the 1v1 trade post-second-item when your W heal is outracing his true damage. If you bled two or more kills in laning phase, this late window narrows sharply — Olaf with a gold lead still runs you down even at full items. Win the resource game, not the ego game early.
edits.after: Two items in, the matchup finally tips. Your AP and W healing compound past his true-damage scaling; stolen Ragnarok gives you the same disable immunity he has; and your chain-passive auto burst in a prolonged brawl outlasts a Tough It Out shield that only lasts a few seconds per cast. The realistic path here is: survive lane without falling more than one kill behind, control vision so he cannot run off to side-lane freely, and take the 1v1 post-second-item when your W heal is outracing his true damage. If you bled two or more kills in laning phase, this late window narrows sharply — Olaf with a gold lead still runs you down even at full items. Win the resource game, not the ego game early.

notes: The kit file flags Undertow with 'grounding'. That is a tooltip-parsing artifact from 'throws an axe into the ground' — Riot's description gives only armour shred, damage and a slow — so no grounding-denies-your-dash advice was written. The mirror reached the same conclusion independently.
